bad.title: Polish on the wrong question
bad.text: Downloading · 62% shows progress, not how long is left, and time left is the problem.

bad.title: Time left, hidden in a sketch
bad.text: The direction that fits the brief looks unfinished, so it’s easy to pass over.

good.title: The ring scores 1 on time left
good.text: It shows progress, not time, on the criterion that counts three times.
good.wait: Press Score against the brief to see this.

good.title: The plain sketch totals 27
good.text: “About 4 min left” earns a 5 where it matters most. The ring totals 16.
good.wait: Press Score against the brief to see this.

good.title: Pick waits for the scores
good.text: Every Pick stays off until each direction is scored, so polish can’t decide first.

bad.title: Scores in view before any weight
bad.text: Trash with restore leads with 27, and every slider move shows who it helps.

bad.title: Weights with no source
bad.text: Nothing ties ×3 for Prevents loss to the brief, so it can slide to suit a favorite.

bad.title: Undo toast wins, after the fact
bad.text: Drop Prevents loss to ×1, raise Low effort, and the favorite comes out on top.
bad.wait: Move the weights until Undo toast wins to see this.

good.title: Each weight cites the brief
good.text: ×3 for Prevents loss, because people lose files by mistake, written before any score.

good.title: Lock comes before the scores
good.text: The sliders freeze, then the totals appear, so nobody can tune them to a favorite.

good.title: Trash with restore wins on its own
good.text: 27 against 23 and 19, with weights nobody could adjust after seeing them.
good.wait: Press Lock weights and show scores to see this.

bad.title: One point is the whole lead
bad.text: 24 against 23, built from judgment calls, is too close to settle anything.

bad.title: “Winner” ends the discussion early
bad.text: The label settles it before anyone asks whether a small change would flip it.

good.title: A one-step test of the weights
good.text: Predictable order drops from ×2 to ×1 to see if the lead holds.

good.title: Recently used now leads, 21 to 19
good.text: The winner flipped, so the two are close and the call rests on a risk.

good.title: The deciding risk, named
good.text: Slow finding matters most here, so Recently used is chosen and the reason is stated.

bad.title: The problem row counts ×1
bad.text: Showing which workflow is running weighs exactly as much as Has animation.

bad.title: Side issues add up to a win
bad.text: One-point leads on Looks modern, brand colors and mobile outweigh 5 against 2 on the problem.

good.title: The problem row counts ×3
good.text: A 5 against 2 on the problem itself now outweighs everything else.

good.title: Badge on tab wins by 8
good.text: The lead comes from the criterion the problem is about, with only four rows to weigh.

bad.title: A picture of a dialog
bad.text: Nothing in it can be clicked or tabbed, so the keyboard path goes unseen.

bad.title: Two bugs reach people
bad.text: Tab never reaches Save, and an empty name gets saved.

good.title: The real dialog, live
good.text: Tab from Cancel leaves the dialog, so the skipped Save shows up at once.

good.title: An empty name, caught early
good.text: Clearing Product shots and pressing Save stores a blank name, with no error.
good.wait: Clear the name and press Save to see this.

bad.title: One state out of four
bad.text: Only With data was shown. Empty, loading and error never came up.

bad.title: Blank on a first visit
bad.text: And when the network fails, the panel spins forever with no way out.

good.title: Four states, one click each
good.text: With data, Empty, Loading and Error can each be opened before approving.

good.title: Empty shows a blank panel
good.text: Found before release, so people never see a screen that looks broken.

good.title: All four seen, two problems found
good.text: The blank panel and the endless spinner get fixed before anyone hits them.
good.wait: Open every state to see this.

bad.title: 15px padding, 7px corners
bad.text: Each is one off from the tokens, with a custom fill. By eye it’s the same Save.

bad.title: Copied into Export and Share
bad.text: A month later, two near-matching button styles exist and nobody knows which is right.

good.title: 3 near misses, found
good.text: Padding 15px against 16px, corners 7px against 8px, and a fill that isn’t color-primary.
good.wait: Press Check against tokens to see this.

good.title: Rebuilt from the tokens
good.text: It now uses space-4, radius-md and color-primary, like the existing Save.
good.wait: Press Check against tokens, then Use the tokens to see this.

bad.title: One problem per round
bad.text: Four problems mean four rounds, each one waiting on the agent.

bad.title: Escape breaks again in round 3
bad.text: Fixing the faint text rewrote the key handling, so an earlier fix came undone.
bad.wait: Press Send next problem until none are left to see this.

good.title: All four in one message
good.text: The agent sees every problem at once, so one fix can’t quietly undo another.

good.title: Checks that guard the fixes
good.text: If a later change breaks Escape again, the Playwright test fails before anyone notices.

good.title: One round, done
good.text: All four fixed, the keyboard test passes and both screenshots come back.
good.wait: Press Send the list to see this.

bad.title: Directions come as whole packages
bad.text: Picking A brings its one long list and name-only choosing along too.

bad.title: 1 of 3 strong, whichever is picked
bad.text: A, B and C each have one strong part, so any whole pick keeps two weak ones.

good.title: Each part picked on its own
good.text: Browsing can come from B’s grid while starting stays with A’s button.

good.title: 3 of 3 strong
good.text: Start from A, browse from B, choose from C. No weak part survives.
good.wait: Pick the strongest option in each row to see this.

bad.title: A sound for every comment
bad.text: It plays for all comments, not just mentions, so it adds noise instead of signal.

bad.title: Six parts, two that help
bad.text: Only the bell count and the highlight help people notice a mention.

bad.title: Six things to learn in one panel
bad.text: Two switches, a tab and reactions crowd the two rows that matter.

good.title: The problem decides what stays
good.text: Each idea gets one test: does it help people notice a mention?

good.title: 2 parts to build
good.text: Down from 6, and both parts left solve the problem.
good.wait: Untick the four parts that don’t help with mentions to see this.

good.title: Bell count and highlight only
good.text: People see who mentioned them and where, with nothing else to learn.
good.wait: Untick the four parts that don’t help with mentions to see this.

bad.title: One “or” gives it away
bad.text: The story needs two ways back, a sign the parts came from different directions.

bad.title: “You can’t get it back”
bad.text: The dialog says the delete is final, yet a toast offers Undo right after.
bad.wait: Press the trash icon on a photo to see this.

good.title: One sentence, no “or”
good.text: The whole flow reads as one path, from delete to Undo.

good.title: Gone at once, Undo on the toast
good.text: One step to delete, and the way back is there if it was a mistake.
good.wait: Press the trash icon on a photo to see this.

bad.title: Says what shipped, not what didn’t
bad.text: Regex patterns were cut, but the pull request never mentions them.

bad.title: The same debate starts over
bad.text: Nobody remembers why regex was dropped, so it goes back in with no new evidence.
bad.wait: Press Two weeks later to see this.

good.title: Regex cut, with the evidence
good.text: None of 40 support requests asked for it, and it’s hard to explain.

good.title: Settled in three messages
good.text: The reason is on record, so regex waits until new requests show up.
good.wait: Press Two weeks later to see this.
